case_name: Uptron India Limited v Shammi Bhan and Another
respondent:
Shammi Bhan and Another
Supreme Court of India

6 February 1998
S.L.P. (C) No. 1079 of 1998
The Judgment was delivered by : S. Saghir Ahmad, J.
1.  Respondent 1 was appointed as an operator (Trainee) on 13.6.1980 in the petitioner's establishment. On completion of training, she was absorbed on that post with effect from 13.7.1981 and was confirmed on 13.7.1982. She thus acquired the status of a permanent employee.
2.  With effect from 7th of November, 1984, respondent 1 proceeded, and remained till 29th January, 1985, on maternity leave. Thereafter, she allegedly remained absent with effect from 30.1.1985 to 12.4.1985 without any application for leave and consequently, by order dated 12th April, 1985, the petitioner informed respondent 1 that her services stood automatically terminated in terms of Clause 17 (g) of the Certified standing Orders. Respondent 1 raised an Industrial Dispute and made prayer to the State Government in 1985 that her case may be referred
holding: The termination of services without providing an opportunity of hearing to the employee would be bad.
The definition of 'Retrenchment' means the termination by the employer of the service of a workman for any reason whatsoever, otherwise than as a punishment inflicted by way of disciplinary action.
The termination of services does not fall in either of the two situations contemplated by Clause (bb) and therefore the finding recorded by the Tribunal on 'retrenchment' cannot be disturbed.
